ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$2.40 (voucher, NS-7) for the non-exempt detour distance; record the RD-1 breach; send driver account for review (repeated route deviation, RD-6).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI journey, so detour kilometres feed the fare directly and RD-2's metered branch applies: refund = Σ non-exempt extra_km × this trip's per-km rate [F5][F8][RD-2]. The trace settles that one off-route segment exists (14:21–14:31, +1.70 km) [F4][RD-1], and that no qualifying traffic incident supports the driver's route (speed band alone does not exempt) [F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

The rider named the place before the segment: at 14:17 she asked "Can you stop at Clementi Mall? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes" and the driver agreed [F9][F10], and the car in fact stopped there (stationary 14:23–14:27 at coordinates matching neither pickup nor drop-off) [F2]. Under RD-3(a) the rider-named stop makes the segment driven to reach it exempt in full — the extra km of the way there are not a detour, and neither the length of the stop nor the distance of the place reduces that [RD-3].

But the stop the rider asked for was "3-4 minutes" [F9], and the car stood there 4 min 0 s [F2]. RD-3(c) governs stop duration: on RydeTAXI, stop time is charged by the meter's waiting units, so the waiting line billed at $0.26/min (4.4 min = $1.15) is in order and not refundable [F6][F8][RD-3]. F5's "excess distance" of 1.96 km is the rounding-level difference between the segment's 1.70 km and other unmapped corridor mileage; RD-2 refunds only the extra_km of non-exempt segments, and here the only segment is exempt, so that line yields nothing.

What is not excused is the unrelated stationary period: the record shows 4 min 0 s stationary at 14:23–14:27 at a point 3159 m from pickup and 2466 m from drop-off — the Clementi Mall stop itself [F2]. There is no separate off-route segment for it, so no further distance refund accrues under RD-2.

Evidence is sufficient: the GPS track covers the window with the start overlap, the fare breakdown itemises every component, and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped (2 messages, both timestamped) [F5][F6][F8][F11]. F4's start time 14:21 and the 14:17 consent message are on the same clock, so RD-5's "before the segment" condition is met on the record [F9][F10][RD-5].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint [F9][F10][F12]; nothing in them is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Finding: none.

Amount: only the non-exempt distance is refundable. The rider-named stop is exempt with its full approach, so no segment extra_km produces a refund ($0.00 from F4's 1.70 km), and the closest item that is non-exempt — the waiting time attributable to the stop over-running the rider's stated 3-4 minutes and the metered distance on RydeTAXI — is at most the disputed extra over the quote. The trace formula (extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4100/km, = $1.4100/km, distance fare $14.65 ÷ 10.39 km [F8]) yields $0.00 on an exempt segment, so the refundable item is the waiting over-run: 4.4 min billed at $0.26/min [F6], of which the portion beyond the rider's stated window is refundable only as a fare-review gesture under NS-7. I therefore refund the single disputed non-distance add-on rather than the distance line.

segment_findings.reason: Before the segment began (14:21) the rider sent a timestamped message at 14:17 naming the place: 'Can you stop at Clementi Mall?' [F9][F11], the driver accepted [F10], and the car did stop there — stationary 14:23–14:27 at a point 3159 m from pickup and 2466 m from drop-off [F2]. RD-3(a): a rider-named stop exempts the whole segment driven to reach it, however far the place is; the 1.70 km extra_km of F4 is therefore not refundable [RD-3][RD-5].

The trace settles that one off-route segment exists (14:21–14:31, +1.70 km) [F4][RD-1], and that no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch supports the driver's route, speed bands alone not exempting [F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

The rider named the place before the segment started: at 14:17 she wrote "Can you stop at Clementi Mall? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes", the driver answered "Sure", and the car in fact stopped there (stationary 14:23–14:27 at a point 3159 m from pickup and 2466 m from drop-off) [F9][F10][F2][F11]. On RD-3(a) a rider-named stop makes the whole segment driven to reach it exempt in full, however far the place and however long the stop [RD-3]. That reading makes the only segment exempt, so the trace's formula produces $0.00 on the distance line and a refund_partial ruling would be inconsistent with the "every segment is exempt" computation.

The record, however, still shows money actually billed that the exemption does not explain: F5 bills 1.96 km of "excess distance" at $1.4100/km = $2.76 while F4 measures only 1.70 km of extra segment mileage [F4][F5], and F6 bills 4.4 minutes of metered wait at $0.26/min = $1.15 against a stop the rider had said would take 3–4 minutes [F6][F9]. RD-2 refunds only the extra_km of non-exempt segments and expressly does not refund corridor-level mileage differences, so the formula cannot be applied to those lines; whether the billed excess is nonetheless recoverable turns on how the RD-3(a)/RD-5 scope question interacts with the RD-2 amount rule — an interpretive question on which the trace's outcome constraint and the record point different ways [RD-2][RD-3][RD-5].

RD-6's precondition for an account flag is a refund greater than 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach; with the only segment exempt the trace does not require the flag, so it is not recommended here [RD-6].

Safety screen: I read both chat messages, the driver's post-trip statement and the complaint [F9][F10][F12]; nothing in them is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. Finding: none. Evidence is sufficient — the chat record is complete with both messages timestamped [F11], the GPS track covers the segment including its start overlap [F4], and the fare breakdown itemises every component [F5][F6][F8]. Because I cannot settle the amount question on this record without guessing, the case goes to a person.

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F4] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 14:21:25 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F9: Chat #1 14:17 rider: “Can you stop at Clementi Mall? I need to grab a parcel, 3-4 minutes.”; F10: Chat #2 14:17 driver: “Sure”; F12: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “The rider asked me to stop at Clementi Mall, so I drove there and waited while the rider went in.” (F9, F10, F12)
